questions.q: Per this lesson, what does the chosen operating model do to the set of possible reference architectures?
options: It rules out some patterns and strongly favors others, because architecture must mirror the authority structure
It has no effect at all on which pattern fits
It makes every pattern equally viable regardless of structure
It requires the architecture to be chosen before the operating model
questions.explain: The lesson states the model constrains which reference-architecture pattern fits, since architecture has to mirror the authority structure.

questions.q: Which reference-architecture pattern does centralized governance pair with, per this lesson?
options: Hub-and-spoke
Mesh of catalogs
Catalog-of-catalogs
No shared pattern at all
questions.explain: Centralized governance pairs with hub-and-spoke: one team, one central hub, every platform feeding in.

questions.q: Which pattern does federated governance pair with?
options: Catalog-of-catalogs
Hub-and-spoke
Mesh of catalogs
A fully decentralized, uncoordinated setup
questions.explain: Federated governance pairs with catalog-of-catalogs — a shared index while domains keep local authority.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why does decentralized governance typically have no shared reference architecture at all?
options: Because each team chooses tools independently with no coordination, which is usually a default rather than a deliberate design
Because decentralized governance is architecturally identical to data mesh
Because decentralized governance is illegal under most regulations
Because decentralized governance always uses hub-and-spoke by definition
questions.explain: The lesson states decentralized typically means no shared architecture — an unplanned default, not a fourth legitimate pattern.

questions.q: What does the lesson say happens if you bolt a centralized hub-and-spoke architecture onto a genuinely federated operating model?
options: It undermines the autonomy the federated model is supposed to preserve
Nothing changes — the two are fully interchangeable
It automatically converts the organization to a data mesh
It has no architectural consequence of any kind
questions.explain: The lesson warns that mismatching architecture to model (e.g., a hub-and-spoke under a federated model) undermines the model's intended autonomy.
